scene.note: You write the lines of welcome.cpp, the compiler builds them into a program, and running it prints the window card.

steps.note: Ambrose wants the workshop's welcome on the window card, exactly as the task spells it.
Under Task 1 you add one statement inside main that prints it.
The compiler reads the file and builds the program, or says which line it cannot read.
Running the program prints the welcome on a line of its own.
The hours are two lines, and they go on the card in the order the task gives.
Each line gets its own print, and each one ends its line.
The program runs its statements from the top of main to the bottom.
The terminal shows the two lines, one under the other, not run together.
A line under Task 3 still prints the free cleaning offer the workshop stopped.
The compiler skips every comment, so a line turned into one is not built.
The offer no longer prints, and the line stays in the file in case it comes back.
A comment is a note for the next person who opens the file, like Kasimir.
The compiler skips comments, so your note changes nothing in the program.
The program prints the same lines as before your note.
